findings.premise: Existing BUILD fingerprint freshness is non-overridable, while legacy review blocks and other-party requirements support recorded overrides.
findings.evidence: approveArtifactOwned calls assertFreshBuildReview before processing overrideReview. enforceCodeReviewGate likewise checks readStoredReviewFreshness before enforcement settings and overrides. Later branches record reviewOverride for blocking or missing/other-party reviews. The design correctly distinguishes these policies. findings.premise: Persistent presentation enforcement is new, and the existing matcher, writer lock and fingerprint exclusion mechanism are valid reuse points.
findings.evidence: handleInsrcPresent currently calls workflow.pending and returns presented/notPending without writing. namesPending implements case-insensitive IDs and exact/suffix path matching. withBuildWriter already uses an exclusive .approval-lock with ownership and dead-process recovery. canonicalReviewBuild deletes BUILD_APPROVAL_IDENTITY_EXCLUSIONS before hashing; its current list contains exactly approvedAt, rejectedAt, rejectReason and reviewOverride. findings.action: Extend these mechanisms while retaining the existing BUILD lock identity and ownership behavior.

findings.premise: The proposed approveAmendment signature preserves its existing callers and approval attribution.
findings.evidence: The current signature is approveAmendment(repoPath, amendmentId, approvedBy: string), and its transition writes approvedBy. approveAmendmentById forwards that third string; the CLI service interface and WorkflowsPane also require it. The proposed third argument is instead opts?: { overrideReview?: string }, with no replacement source for approvedBy. The existing test explicitly asserts back.approvedBy === 'alice'. findings.premise: TUI presentation can be implemented solely by wiring workflow.present into an existing document-open event.
findings.evidence: WorkflowsPane opens EpicDetail, which renders chain status and actionable labels. Its input handler directly executes "input === 'a' ... doApprove(focused)"; it never opens or renders the selected artifact document or amendment contents. The service then directly calls approveArtifactByJsonPath. Section 2.9 supplies no new document-view flow or event where the required presentation can occur. findings.action: Design the TUI artifact/amendment open-and-read flow, presentation timing, loading/failure states, expiry recovery and approval enablement. Provide prose or a relevant UX companion sufficient to assess that flow. No rendered companion verification is claimed.

findings.premise: Locking presentation and approval writers is sufficient to prevent cross-worker loss of presentation, rejection and review state.
findings.evidence: Non-BUILD rejectArtifactByJsonPath still performs an unlocked read-modify-write. reviewArtifactFile reads the artifact before awaiting review and later writes "{ ...artifact, meta: { ...artifact.meta, review: stamped }, body: fixed.body }" without the approval lock. resolveReviewFinding also writes the full artifact without it. These writers are absent from the proposed coordination inventory. They can overwrite a newly consumed token or approval, while an approval can overwrite a concurrent rejection using its earlier snapshot. [files: src/workflow/gates.ts, src/workflow/approval-owner.ts, src/workflow/review/run-artifact.ts, src/workflow/review/resolve.ts, docs/standalone/enforce-approval-hard-gates-daemon-present-E2026110350751aa8/S001/LLD.md]
findings.action: Specify coordination or conflict detection for every writer that changes approval-relevant state, including rejection, review publication and review resolution. Require rereading current state at publication and test these competing writers across workers.

findings.premise: Optional embedded presentation fields are compatible with existing record shapes and can preserve the pending-list contract.
findings.evidence: listPendingArtifacts filters ordinary records using approvedAt/rejectedAt and AMD records using status; additional fields do not affect those predicates. Amendment validation permits additional properties. BUILD mergeWithPrior spreads both prior.meta and rec.meta, preserving omitted metadata. The design describes one artifact-owned current presentation, replaced on re-presentation and consumed on approval; prose adequately explains that relationship without an ERD. [files: src/workflow/pending.ts, src/workflow/amendments/types.ts, src/workflow/amendments/store.ts, src/workflow/runners/build/standalone-record.ts]
findings.action: Preserve these readers and metadata merges. Older pending records must acquire a presentation before approval; existing approved records need no presentation backfill. Clarify that rejected AMDs remain terminal under their preserved transition rules.

findings.premise: This is a standalone Story without parent-HLD ownership contracts to redesign.
findings.evidence: The persisted artifact records standalone:true, sizeClass:'feature', hldAmendmentsApplied:[], empty ownedContracts/consumedContracts and no adjacent boundaries. Its scope spans the existing workflow approval layer and its transports/clients, consistent with the recorded standalone triage rationale. findings.action: Keep presentation enforcement in the workflow layer and transport/client changes limited to invoking and surfacing it.

findings.premise: requireFreshPresentation(meta, opts) has enough specified evidence to reject presentations older than the last completed review, including BUILD code reviews.
findings.evidence: BUILD code reviews are published separately as CR-<epic>-<story>; readStoredReviewFreshness explicitly loads that sibling record. Publishing a code review does not stamp its completion into BUILD.meta. The proposed helper receives only ApprovableArtifactMeta and clock/enforcement options, with no sibling-review input or specified completion marker. Furthermore, CR.createdAt is "new Date(startedAtMs).toISOString()", and daemon design reviews receive reviewedAt before the review runs. Those timestamps cannot establish the last review-write time promised by §4. findings.action: Define authoritative review-publication freshness evidence and how the presentation gate receives it, including separate CR records and reviews finishing after presentation. Specify and test rejection of present-during-review followed by review completion and approval.

findings.premise: Every acceptance criterion maps to a test that proves its complete requirement.
findings.evidence: The LLD maps ac1–ac8 to named scenarios, but the criterion definitions were not found. Existing gates, present-dispatch, VS Code fake-IPC and JetBrains fake-RPC tests provide suitable extension points, and ac8 explicitly plans fixture migration. These establish feasibility, not completeness against unavailable criteria. The listed concurrent-client scenario also does not specify the competing review/rejection writers identified above. summary.prose: The daemon refuses approvals that were never presented to the human first, enforced in the one shared approve path every caller funnels through (approveArtifactByJsonPath), with presentation records that are fingerprint-safe for BUILD reviews, single-use, TTL-bound, and serialized per artifact across session workers. insrc_present becomes a write (new daemon RPC workflow.present) wired into every approval surface — MCP tool, VS Code docs review, JetBrains review pane, TUI — at document-open time. epicHash batch approval additionally requires the explicit artifactIds list, so blanket approve-all is refused. Review gates stay exactly as they are, including the non-overridable stale-review fingerprint rule; overrideReview remains present-gated. AMD amendment records get the same treatment through approveAmendment, and rejected records get a defined re-present recovery.

hldContextSlice.frameworkSummary: Standalone feature — no parent HLD. Design directly against the repo, grounded on the s1 analyze passes. There are no HLD shared contracts to honour.
